summary: Multi-select filter chips: selecting floods a chip with dots from the click point and draws a check. Submits one value per chip.

attributes.name: options
attributes.description: Comma-separated chips as `Label:count`, split at the last colon. The count is optional and shown after the label. Observed: a change rebuilds the chips and keeps the selected labels.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Comma-separated labels of the selected chips, matched exactly. Observed: a change updates the selection and becomes the selection a form reset restores. Reflects the current selection.

attributes.name: label
attributes.description: Heading text; also labels the chip group. Observed.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Form field name used when the element is inside a form.

attributes.name: disabled
attributes.description: Presence attribute. Disables every chip and Clear; a disabled ancestor `<fieldset>` does the same. A disabled element is not submitted.

events.name: change
events.description: Fires when the user toggles a chip or presses Clear. `value` lists the selected labels in option order.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Selected labels. Setting accepts an array or a comma-separated string and writes the `value` attribute.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The `name` attribute. There is no setter; set the attribute instead.

accessibility: Each chip is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed` reflecting its state, inside a `role="group"` container labelled by the heading.
The Clear button shows the selected count and is disabled when nothing is selected; when it had focus, focus then moves to the first chip.
The fill and check are drawn on an `aria-hidden` canvas.
motion: With reduced motion, a chip fills and draws its check at once instead of flooding from the click point; the hover tint still eases.
form: With `name`, submits one entry per selected chip under that name; without a name the internal value is the comma-joined labels. There is no validation. Form reset restores the selection from the `value` set by markup or code; a disabled element is not submitted.
notes: Setting `value` through the attribute or the property does not fire `change`. A chip toggled from the keyboard floods from its centre.
Omitting `value` selects TypeScript and Rust; `value=""` starts with nothing selected.
Chips wrap to the host's width.

data.note: Pass your chips and counts as `options` (`Label:count`). Without it the chips show demo languages with invented counts.
